name: Slow Cooker Buffalo Chicken and Rice Bowl
intro_html: This is a full week of buffalo chicken dinners built right in your slow cooker, tangy shredded chicken over rice with a little broccoli and melty cheddar. It hits that wing-night craving with real protein instead of a plate of empty fried stuff, and every gram of protein comes from lean chicken breast. A tray of buffalo wings runs you $12 a person at a bar, and this bowl feeds you the same flavor for a fraction of that.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2495 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 6 lb: ~$12.27. Buy 6 lbs: $13.38.
Ranch Seasoning Mix, 6 3/4 tbsp: ~$0.88. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 1oz packets.
Buffalo Wing Sauce, 1 cup: ~$1.65. Buy 1 (covers this batch with some left over).
Rice, 5.5 cups dry: ~$1.23. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Pantry seasonings (salt): ~$0.01. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $21.60 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.54 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $25.11 across 14 servings, roughly $1.79 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $9.25 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $34.36. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Buy chicken breast in the big family pack. The per-pound price on a 5 to 6 lb pack is almost always lower than small trays, and this recipe uses all of it.
Grab a store-brand ranch seasoning. It tastes the same in a slow cooker as the name brand and costs half as much. Buffalo sauce keeps for months, so watch for it on sale and stock up.
Use frozen broccoli if fresh is pricey that week. Frozen is picked at peak, costs less, and works perfectly here since you are cooking it down anyway.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.

Put the chicken breast in the slow cooker, sprinkle on the ranch seasoning, and pour over the buffalo sauce with the melted butter. Cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or high for 3 to 4, until the chicken pulls apart with a fork.
While that finishes, cook your rice per the package. This is your base and it stretches the whole batch.
Toss the broccoli florets with the olive oil and salt, then roast or steam them until just tender and still bright green. Do not overcook it or it turns to mush by day three.
Shred the chicken while it is still warm, right in the slow cooker, using two forks. Warm chicken shreds far easier than cold.
Toss the shredded chicken back through its own cooking liquid so every bite stays juicy and coated.
Add the cooked rice, broccoli, and the shredded cheddar to your weighed mixing pot and fold everything together.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide that number by 14. Scoop that exact weight into each of your 14 containers so every dinner carries the same hearty serving of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Eating Bird Food, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Fourteen buffalo chicken dinners for two, at a per-bowl cost that beats one order of wings. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
